newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Anzag H1 96/97 sales fall but income rises.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Anzag H1 96/97 sales fall but income rises.

text.p: German drugs wholesaler Andreae-Noris Zahn AG (Anzag) said on Wednesday that its sales for the first half of the 1996/97 financial year had fallen to 2.096 billion marks ($1.2 billion) from 2.139 billion.
But the group said that first-half income from ordinary activities was up 14.2 percent, at 39.0 million marks.
Revenues in the first half of the financial year, which runs from September 1996 to August 1997, were hit by falling demand in the pharmaceuticals market.
Anzag said that it expected total sales in the current year to fall by 1.5 percent to 4.25 billion marks as revenues would be hit by further cutbacks in the state health sector.
"Our sales development is heavily influenced by political decisions," Anzag's chief executive Hermann Franke said in a statement. "Our business can only react to these decisions."
Franke said the firm had altered its cost structure in 1996, and said that the first half results showed that this alteration was correct.
Franke added that despite what he termed a "difficult" business year, the firm still expected to offer an attractive dividend to shareholders.
Anzag upped its dividend for 1995/96 to 18 marks from 14 marks after posting a 19 percent rise in net profit to 38.5 million marks.

Anzag said measures taken in May 1996 to adjust the shareholding structure of the firm and streamline operations had led to a substantial decline in operating expenditure, falling by 5.9 million marks to 151.6 million marks.
Shares in Anzag were unchanged at 615 marks in bourse trade, while the overall market was up 1.65 percent at 3,438.92 points.
